description:
The Blue Carbon Project Bonos del Jaguar Azul is the first project in México to be developed for mangroves under VCS program. It is a project which includes in its expansion region all the mangrove and tropical dry forests located in the Yucatan Peninsula,in the Mexican Caribbean. In a report of the study of Mexican Mangroves, published by the National Commission for Knowledge and Use of Biodiversity in 2009 (CONABIO, 2009), it was concluded that the Yucatan Peninsula contains 55% of the total area of mangroves in Mexico with 423,751 ha, of which the state Yucatan occupies 99,640 ha, mostly protected by federal and state decrees. In the Yucatan Peninsula, mangroves are habitat for numerous animal species such as jaguar, crocodile and many water bird specieslike pink flamingo, wood stork, pelican, roseate spoonbill, white ibis and several species of herons. Some of these species are considered endangered or threatened. 

The principal aim is the removals of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through activities that allow the identification, prioritization and execution of actions for the adequate management of mangroves, the advancement of sustainable development, the establishment of local governance and the promotion of another productive activity, while contributing to the protection of high community values of biodiversity conservation.

The Project began on July, 2016 and will have an expected duration of 30 years; during this period, the reduction of 3,278,919 between mangrove and tropical low deciduous forests is expected through the implementation of activities related to four strategic lines: strengthening of governance, alternative productive projects, recovery and rehabilitation of mangrove areas, and monitoring aerial biomass growth.

This Project Will maintain sustainable community management practices for mangroves and floodable tropical forests, with a greater perception of the value of ecosystem services.
